description: Published a public rate card (Growth 'starting at $3,750/mo, billed annually') — unusual for the category and apparently part of the post-controversy transparency reset (date approximated; reported).

Weekly usage limits added on top of 5-hour rolling sessions for Pro/Max: overall weekly cap plus separate Opus cap. Announced July 28, 2025; effective August 28, 2025. Anthropic stated <5% of users affected; aimed at 24/7 Claude Code use and account sharing. Reported ranges at launch: Pro 40–80 hrs Sonnet 4/week; Max 5x 140–280 hrs Sonnet + 15–35 hrs Opus; Max 20x 240–480 + 24–40 (reported only).
user_reaction: Documented developer backlash, esp. Claude Code power users; later temporary weekly-limit boosts reported into 2026

description: Devin 2.0: entry price dropped from $500/mo minimum (Team: 250 ACUs) to a $20 pay-as-you-go Core plan — a ~96% entry-price cut, widely covered as opening the coding-agent price war.
user_reaction: Positive; framed as commoditization signal

description: Post-Windsurf merge: credit system retired entirely in favor of daily/weekly usage quotas; Windsurf Pro $15→$20; $200 Max tier added; Windsurf pricing merged into unified Devin plans (date reported only; corroborated by live redirect of windsurf.com/pricing).
user_reaction: Mild complaints on the $15→$20 rise; minor vs acquisition drama

description: Pro changed from $20/mo for 500 fast requests to $20/mo API-rate compute credit pool plus unlimited Auto (auto-routed models); Ultra ($200/mo) introduced. Effective usage fell to roughly 225 Sonnet-4 requests vs the former 500. 'Unlimited' applied only to Auto, which was widely misunderstood.
notice_period: none — announced via blog but rollout poorly communicated; clarified June 30
grandfathering: none for the request model; full refunds offered for surprise charges June 16–July 4 via pro-pricing@cursor.com after July 4 public apology ('we missed the mark')
user_reaction: Documented backlash: surprise overages (reports of $350+/week), mass complaints, public apology and refunds

description: 'Updates to Teams and Auto' — adjustments to Teams plans and Auto usage; Pro+ tier appears on the pricing page in this era (exact launch date not verified from primary source).

Publicly formalized the dual pricing menu: (a) per-conversation — fixed rate per incoming conversation with volume discounts; (b) per-resolution — higher rate, no charge for escalations, commitments lower the rate. Majority of customers reported choosing per-conversation.

Premium-request billing enforcement began (system announced April 2025 with Pro+): allowances per plan (reported: Pro 300/mo, Pro+ 1,500, Business 300/user, Enterprise 1,000/user), overage $0.04/request, per-model multipliers.
user_reaction: Grumbling over multipliers; moderate

description: Unannounced-in-advance tightening of Individual plan limits and pause on self-serve Business signups.
user_reaction: Community discussion backlash (#192963)

description: Premium request units replaced by GitHub AI Credits consumed by token usage (input+output+cached) at published per-model API rates; completions/Next Edit exempt; model fallback removed. Announced April 27, 2026. Annual Pro/Pro+ subscribers keep premium-request pricing until expiry BUT with increased model multipliers from June 1 — partial silent degradation of grandfathered terms.
grandfathering: partial — legacy pricing retained for annual subs with worsened multipliers
user_reaction: Documented backlash: 'you will get less, but pay the same price'

description: I/O 2026: Ultra restructured — new $100/mo Ultra tier (5x limits) introduced and top tier cut from $249.99 to $200/mo. Lineage: Feb 2024 'Google One AI Premium' $19.99 → May 2025 rebrand to AI Pro + Ultra launch at $249.99 → Jan 2026 Plus tier ($7.99) → these cuts. One Premium subscribers grandfathered with 2TB.
user_reaction: Positive

description: AI Plus cut from $7.99 (Jan 2026 launch price) to $4.99/mo with storage doubled to 400GB.
user_reaction: Positive

description: Growth repositioned from ~$37/mo to $47 monthly ($37.60 annual), with new bundle SKUs (Starter/Scale/Agency) — effective increase via repackaging; date approximated, reported only.
user_reaction: Third-party pricing guides flagged the shift

description: Free tier (400 credits/mo) discontinued; credit numbers dropped from public tiers; relaunched as Plus/Pro/Max assistant plans with vague usage multiples (date approximated within Jan–Mar 2026 window; reported only). Prior: Pro $49.99 ≈ 5,000 credits, Business $299 ≈ 30,000 credits.
user_reaction: Third-party guides flagged the opacity increase

description: Shift from flat message counts to fractional complexity-based credits with daily credits and rollover (iterative rollout through 2025; exact date approximated to mid-2025 — reported only, docs changelog). Original late-2024 launch was $20/mo near-unlimited messaging, then message counts, then credits.
user_reaction: Modest recurring complaints about credit burn on errors; no single backlash event

description: Paid launch: Starter $39/mo (3,900 credits), Pro $199/mo (19,900 credits). Later restructured to the current 'Pro' ladder (from $20/4,000 credits) with explicit grandfathering for existing members at unchanged prices.
grandfathering: full — existing members auto-renew at unchanged prices (primary help center)
user_reaction: Launch complaints about credit burn and no upfront task estimates

description: Video V1 launch: video jobs cost ~8x an image job in GPU time (reported figure — Holz statement); unlimited Relax video added to Pro/Mega. Headline plan prices unchanged — a capability-expansion that repriced effective usage.
user_reaction: Fast-hour burn complaints from video users

description: Comet browser — launched July 2025 as a Max-gated ($200/mo) product — made free on all platforms. Comet Plus publisher-content add-on $5/mo (reported).
user_reaction: Positive

description: 'Effort-Based Pricing' replaced flat $0.25/checkpoint — simple tasks under $0.25, complex tasks bundled into one variable-priced checkpoint. Applied to existing subscribers July 1, 2025.
user_reaction: Initial acceptance; complaints grew with Agent 3

description: Agent 3 launch triggered cost-unpredictability backlash: users reported ~$1,000/week vs prior $180–200/month, single prompts costing $20, no pre-run estimate, and billing for failed/looping runs. Replit's FAQ disclaims the agent is 'probabilistic... may occasionally make mistakes.'
notice_period: n/a — product launch with existing meter
user_reaction: Documented backlash (The Register, InfoWorld)

description: 'Unlimited' plan ($76/mo: 2,250 credits + unlimited throttled Explore Mode) retired, replaced by credit-only Max (9,500 credits, no Explore Mode) — an 'unlimited'-to-metered conversion. Date approximated 2025/26; reported only.
user_reaction: Complaints from heavy Explore Mode users (reported)

description: SuperGrok Heavy launched at $300/mo — multi-agent Grok 4 Heavy, top-tier limits; at the time the most expensive consumer AI subscription.
user_reaction: Sticker-shock commentary

description: Free tier lost all Imagine image/video generation — a quiet removal; SuperGrok Lite ($10/mo) launched days later (Mar 25) as the new entry point for generation features.
user_reaction: User complaints about the silent removal

description: AI by Zapier steps repriced by model tier: Standard 1x, Advanced 3x (default), Premium 5x tasks per run; tool calls billed additively.
notice_period: announced via help center in advance

description: Pay-per-task overage rates raised for monthly plans.
grandfathering: monthly plans affected; annual unaffected until renewal
